Title: Disable font-not-found warning if alternative font is found. #6010
Author: 
Published Date: 2025-03-05T00:00:00.000Z
URL: https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/6010
Text: Description 
 I have written a template that uses the CMU fonts. However, on some systems, there is only the alternative Font "New Computer Modern" available and vice versa. Both Fonts are almost the same (at least for Latin characters), so either is a perfectly valid choice for all use-cases I have. Therefore, in my template I have the following code: 
 set text(
font: (
"CMU Sans Serif",
"New Computer Modern Sans",
),
size: 12pt,
) 
 Unfortunately, since #2818 this produces the following warning on systems where only one of these font families is installed: 
 warning: unknown font family: new computer modern sans
┌─ template/foobar.typ:105:10
│
105 │ font: (
│ ╭───────────^
106 │ │ "CMU Sans Serif",
107 │ │ "New Computer Modern Sans",
108 │ │ ),
│ ╰─────^
 
 Maybe I'm following an antipattern here, but I think it'd be great if the warning is only thrown if no valid font (for actually used character sets) is found. 
 Use Case 
 Described above.

Title: Throw error when there are no fonts. · Issue #5399 · typst/typst - GitHub
Author: typst
Published Date: 2024-11-10T00:00:00.000Z
URL: https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/5399
Text: I was using the typst crate in Rust. I created my own World, and for the fonts I embedded the standard fonts from the typst-assets crate. However, somehow my test files which contained some simple markup were not rendering. It would just layout an empty page. The weird thing, though, was that there were no errors or warnings, and all Rust functions returned with Ok(...). After a long time of debugging, I found the problem: 
 
 When I thought I was loading the embedded fonts I did in fact not load anything, because I didn't activate the fonts feature of typst-assets. I had an empty font book. 
 So I suggest: 
 
 Throw an error when the font book is empty. (Or when the requested font, in this case "Libertinus Serif", is not present in the font book.) 
 Hide the whole fonts() function in typst-assets under the respective feature flag. That I was able to call typst_assets::fonts() gave me a false sense of security. It took me a long time until I was looking at the docs of that function which told me it returns an empty iterator if the feature is
